source.title: Neural Characteristic Activation Analysis and Geometric Parameterization for ReLU Networks

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Compares training accuracy over epochs for VGG-6 under multiple parameterizations, bearing on V6's training-speed claim using a different architecture and benchmark.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a training-accuracy curve for VGG-6 on ImageNet32 (Figure 4a). The text describes validation-accuracy convergence speed but does not give numerical training-accuracy values. Its other reported accuracy and RMSE results are validation or test performance, not training classification error or the behaviors named by the other versions.
record.test_reason: The VGG-6 experiment compares accuracy convergence with and without BN on ImageNet32, a new setting for V6. Validation accuracy over epochs bears on gaining accuracy faster; V6 does not require training accuracy exclusively.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate as a summary of the authors' conclusion: their analysis identifies activation-boundary instability, and they report that GmP improves stability, convergence speed and generalization across evaluated architectures and tasks. These are reported advantages, not uniform wins on every benchmark.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates geometric parameterization, comparing it with standard parameterization, weight normalization, and batch normalization; it does not use the claim versions' recipes as its focus.
record.method_sensitivity: For VGG-6 on ImageNet32, the reported optimal initial learning rate is 0.1 for GmP and 0.01 for the other compared methods. Batch size and input mean normalization are also varied or compared.

fits_no_version.finding: BN and other Cartesian parameterizations can exhibit large characteristic activation-boundary changes under small parameter perturbations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-boundary sensitivity depends on parameterization and weight magnitude.

fits_no_version.finding: GmP+IMN reaches validation convergence within 25 epochs, approximately 10 epochs before BN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GmP+IMN can accelerate validation convergence relative to BN in VGG-6 on ImageNet32.

record.problems: The training-accuracy comparison is presented only as a plot, without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The textual convergence-speed comparison is for validation accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for Figure 4(b) validation accuracy: it is not training accuracy as named by V6. Other benchmark accuracy and RMSE results measure validation or test performance rather than training error or training speed.

untested.parts: Near-zero CIFAR training classification error, including corrupted labels and size or regularization dependencies.
Teacher-student spurious minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts or the specified alternatives.
Initialization comparisons measuring learning speed or trainable depth. Initialization remarks do not provide those comparisons.
Loss recovery, curvature and divergence relative to a measured stability threshold.
Fixup; higher learning-rate tolerance from adding BN. Cross-validation selects 0.01 for both SP and BN on ImageNet32, which does not establish their maximum stable rates.

missing.what: Correct the exclusion declared in rows_left_out: validation accuracy over epochs does measure V6's accuracy-speed component. Record the SP versus BN convergence comparison; the text ranks BN second fastest and places its convergence at approximately 35 epochs, without specifying SP's convergence epoch.

record.verdict_notes: The validation result is explicitly declared omitted, so the missing entry corrects that exclusion rather than identifying an undisclosed omission. Neither BN's perturbation sensitivity nor GmP's superior performance contradicts the narrower claim that adding BN accelerates accuracy gains.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training error, random or corrupted labels, model size, stopping and regularization.
Two-layer teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima, and student width.
Depth-related training error, identity shortcuts, Fixup, and plain deep networks.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Training above stability thresholds, curvature, and divergence.

The paper compares training-accuracy curves for VGG-6 on ImageNet32, but gives no numerical values for that measure; its textual convergence-speed result concerns validation accuracy. It does not test Fixup.

rows.note: Curve is shown without numerical values or a textual description of its comparison with the other methods.

rows.subject: VGG-6 (GmP)

rows.note: Curve is shown without numerical values or a textual description of its comparison with the other methods.

rows.subject: VGG-6 (GmP+IMN)

rows.note: Curve is shown without numerical values or a textual description of its comparison with the other methods.
rows.check: GmP+IMN is the study's proposed method, not Fixup. Outperforming BN does not establish that BN fails to accelerate the standard network.

relationships.condition: VGG-6 on ImageNet32, batch size 1024; validation-accuracy convergence over epochs.
relationships.reason: Section 4.2.2 explicitly ranks BN second fastest among the compared methods, ahead of SP; BN converges at approximately 35 epochs. This verdict uses the text, not unreadable training curves R1 and R4, and requires the validation rows incorrectly excluded by the record.
relationships.display_finding: Batch normalization converged in approximately 35 epochs, ranking second fastest among the compared methods and ahead of SP.
